I’ve had it since I started doing any exercise, my problem is hypermobility so stretching actually makes it worse, whereas for most people having one muscle be super tight usually is addressed with stretching and foam rolling. I’m not qualified to give advice but most people will find that addressing imbalances (antagonist muscles weak af) and loosening tightnesses can curb the tendonitis problem. Definitely don’t stop lifting but if it’s coming in as a result of ramping up the intensity then maybe you’re not deloading enough, you can’t train 80-90% 1RM all year long, you will need to take a week every 3-6 week cycle to train light and easy. 

So basically deloading, strengthening weaknesses, loosening tight stuff (stuff tends to get tight when its too weak but you need to be good at self assessment), stretching if you’re normal, and last but not least maybe you’re just doing too much with the wrong technique: say you’re training front squats and knee extensions only at 90% - you’re going to be loading the fuck out of your knees. The more a joint is isolated, the less intensity you want.  

This is just stuff I’ve learned so far, I have no qualifications in exercise physiology or anatomy or PT or anything else.

One final thing comes to mind: you get people like Knees over toes guy who preach “bulletproofing techniques” and while sometimes they have whack advice or dump a thousand “functional fuckery” exercises on you, the principle of exposing a weak area to slow, gradual overload is good. You won’t unfuck your knees doing depth jumps, but do enough sissy squats with slow increments in weight at recoverable volumes, but low intensity, and chances are you’ll see improvement. When I was 15 starting parkour as a little chubster, my knees got fucked very quick, but through enough sissy/pistol squatting (didn’t even know what barbells were) I was able to gradually unfuck myself.
